items.title: @astrojs/vercel: ISR routes can serve a cached redirect to /$0 when Vercel doesn't substitute the undocumented $0 token

labels.name: - P4: important
labels.description: Violate documented behavior or significantly impacts performance (priority)

labels.name: triage: fix verified
labels.description: Reporter confirmed the triage bot fix works

items.body:
### Astro Info

```block
Astro                    v7.3.2
Node                     v24.18.0
System                   Linux (x64) / Vercel
Package Manager          npm
Output                   server
Adapter                  @astrojs/vercel v11.0.10
Integrations             (not relevant — the generated route table reproduces independently of integrations)
```

Relevant config: `output: 'server'`, `trailingSlash: 'always'`, `vercel({ isr: { expiration: <n>, bypassToken: … } })`.

### If this issue only occurs in one browser, which browser is a problem?

_No response — this is server-side._

### Describe the Bug

In production on Vercel, valid ISR pages intermittently return a `301` to a URL containing the **literal, un-substituted** `$0` capture token:

```
GET  https://<site>/<some>/<valid>/<isr-path>/
→ 301 https://<site>/$0/?x_astro_path=%240
```

The response carries a stale `date` header and a large `age` (observed ~17,900s), i.e. it is served from cache rather than recomputed. It affects a subset of regions at a time and clears on redeploy.

#### Root cause

`getIsrPath` writes `$0` into the `dest` of every ISR route ([`packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/withastro/astro/blob/main/packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts)):

```ts
// This isn't documented by vercel anywhere, but unlike serverless
// and edge functions, isr functions are not passed the original path.
// Instead, we have to use $0 to refer to the regex match from "src".
const getIsrPath = (pathToken: string) =>
	`/_isr?${ASTRO_PATH_PARAM}=$0&${ASTRO_PATH_TOKEN_PARAM}=${pathToken}`;
```

The comment already flags the core risk: **this relies on undocumented Vercel behaviour.** Vercel's own reference router explicitly excludes `$0` from substitution — [`packages/cli/src/util/dev/router.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/blob/main/packages/cli/src/util/dev/router.ts):

```ts
export function resolveRouteParameters(str, match, keys) {
  return str.replace(/\$([1-9a-zA-Z]+)/g, (_, param) => { ... });
}
```

Note the character class `[1-9a-zA-Z]` — zero is not in it. (`$0` is also not special in JS replacement-string semantics, which only honours `$1`–`$99`, `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'`.) The production proxy evidently does special-case `$0`, since this works the vast majority of the time — but there is no documented guarantee, and when it doesn't happen the failure mode is silent and long-lived.

#### Why it fails silently

The entrypoint accepts whatever is in `x_astro_path` without validation ([`src/serverless/entrypoint.ts`](https://github.com/withastro/astro/blob/main/packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts)):

```ts
realPath = url.searchParams.get(ASTRO_PATH_PARAM);   // → "$0"
if (typeof realPath === 'string') {
	const target = new URL(realPath, url);
	url.pathname = target.pathname;                    // → "/$0"
```

`"$0"` is a syntactically valid *relative* URL, so `new URL()` doesn't throw — it resolves against the `/_isr` base and yields `/$0`:

```js
const url = new URL('https://example.com/_isr?x_astro_path=$0&x_astro_path_token=abc');
new URL(url.searchParams.get('x_astro_path'), url).pathname;
// → '/$0'
```

Astro then renders `/$0`, and with `trailingSlash: 'always'` a redirect to `/$0/` is emitted.

Note that `x_astro_path_token` does **not** guard against this: the token is a literal in the `dest` string, so it substitutes correctly even when `$0` does not. The check passes and the bad path is accepted.

#### Why one bad response causes hours of breakage

`buildISRFolder` writes:

```ts
allowQuery: [ASTRO_PATH_PARAM, ASTRO_PATH_TOKEN_PARAM],
passQuery: true,
```

Every route in the app rewrites to the same function path, `/_isr`. The only thing separating one page's cache entry from another's is `x_astro_path`. So `x_astro_path=$0` is just another valid cache key, and the resulting redirect is stored and replayed for the whole configured `expiration` window, per region, until the next deployment. Any CDN in front then caches that 301 against the *real* page URL.

So a rare substitution failure is amplified into a multi-hour, partial-region outage.

### What's the expected result?

A request for a valid ISR route returns `200`. If the path override can't be trusted, the adapter should fail closed rather than render — and must not produce a cacheable redirect to a nonsense path.

#### Suggested fixes

Either one alone closes the hole; (a) is the root-cause fix, (b) is cheap defence in depth and arguably worth having regardless.

**(a) Stop depending on `$0`.** Wrap the pattern in an outer capture group and use `$1`, which *is* within Vercel's documented substitution range. The inner groups from `route.patternRegex.source` are never referenced by `dest`, so shifting their indices is harmless:

```
src:  "^\\/([^/]+?)\\/([^/]+?)\\/$"
  →   "^(\\/([^/]+?)\\/([^/]+?)\\/)$"
dest: "/_isr?x_astro_path=$1&x_astro_path_token=…"
```

**(b) Validate `realPath` in the entrypoint.** A correctly substituted path always starts with `/`, because `patternRegex.source` is anchored with `^\/`. The literal `$0` does not:

```diff
-if (typeof realPath === 'string') {
+if (typeof realPath === 'string' && realPath.startsWith('/')) {
```

This turns a silent cache poisoning into an ordinary request served as `/_isr` — which is what the existing token comment already describes as the intended behaviour ("otherwise the path is ignored and the request is served as `/_isr`").

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

Build-output repro (see steps below) — the runtime half needs Vercel's production proxy and is not deterministic.

#### Reproducing the defect in the generated route table

This part is fully deterministic and needs no deployment:

1. `npm create astro@latest` (minimal template)
2. `npx astro add vercel`
3. Set `output: 'server'` and configure the adapter with `isr: { expiration: 60 }`
4. Add any dynamic page, e.g. `src/pages/[a]/[b].astro`
5. `npx astro build`
6. Inspect `.vercel/output/config.json`

Every non-prerendered route's `dest` contains the literal `$0`:

```json
{ "src": "^/([^/]+?)/([^/]+?)/$", "dest": "/_isr?x_astro_path=$0&x_astro_path_token=…" }
```

The Node snippet in the bug description reproduces the entrypoint's silent acceptance of that token. What can't be reproduced on demand is the proxy-side substitution failure itself — that is internal to Vercel's edge and non-deterministic. I'm happy to provide more production evidence (headers, timings) if useful.

### Participation

- [ ] I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.

items.title: @astrojs/vercel: `middlewareMode: 'edge'` is silently inert when `isr` is enabled

labels.name: triage: unable to reproduce
labels.description: Triage bot attempted reproduction but could not reproduce

items.body:
### Astro Info

```block
Astro                    v7.2.2
Node                     v24.18.1
System                   Linux (x64)
Package Manager          pnpm
Output                   server
Adapter                  @astrojs/vercel v11.0.5
Integrations             none
```

### If this issue only occurs in one browser, which browser is a problem?

_No response_

### Describe the Bug

With `@astrojs/vercel`, setting both `middlewareMode: 'edge'` and `isr` produces a
`_middleware` edge function that is built, bundled and deployed, but that no page
route ever invokes. The option silently does nothing.

In `packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts`, the non-ISR branch points every
on-demand route at the middleware (`dest = _middlewareEntryPoint ? MIDDLEWARE_PATH : NODE_PATH`).
The ISR branch points them at the ISR function instead, so `MIDDLEWARE_PATH` survives
only for `isr.exclude` entries and the 404 catch-all. `buildMiddlewareFolder()` is then
called regardless, so the edge function is produced and uploaded either way.

Generated `.vercel/output/config.json` for a fixture with `middlewareMode: 'edge'` plus
`isr: { expiration: 120 }` and nothing else:

```json
{ "src": "^/$",      "dest": "/_isr?x_astro_path=$0&x_astro_path_token=…" },
{ "src": "^/404/?$", "dest": "/_isr?x_astro_path=$0&x_astro_path_token=…" },
{ "src": "^/.*$",    "dest": "_middleware", "status": 404 }
```

The only route pointing at `_middleware` is the 404 catch-all.

The runtime consequence is that middleware only runs inside the ISR function — Vercel's
ISR caches on the path and, on a cache hit, does not invoke the function at all. So any
middleware on an ISR-enabled Vercel site stops running once an entry is warm: security
headers, redirects, auth gates, geo, A/B, content negotiation. Running ahead of the cache
is the reason edge middleware exists, and the one configuration where it is needed is the
one where the routing to it is dropped.

Observed on a live site (`output: 'server'`, `isr: { expiration: 86400 }`,
`edgeMiddleware: true`) that negotiates HTML vs. Markdown on `/` from the `Accept`
header:

```console
$ curl -sI -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://<site>/
content-type: text/html          # should be text/markdown
x-vercel-cache: HIT              # the middleware never ran
age: 535
```

Its build output contained a 1.9 MB `_middleware.func` reachable from nothing but 404s.

### What's the expected result?


Either of:

1. **Minimum:** the adapter warns (or throws) at build time when `isr` and
   `middlewareMode: 'edge'` are both set, instead of shipping a function nothing calls.
2. **Preferred:** on-demand routes are pointed at `MIDDLEWARE_PATH` in the ISR branch too, and
   the generated middleware's `next()` forwards to `/_isr?x_astro_path=…&x_astro_path_token=…`
   for ISR-backed routes and `/_render` for routes matched by `isr.exclude`, so cached
   responses are still served while the middleware runs first.

(2) is what PR #17687 implements, with a fixture and route-table assertions. Note the tradeoff
stated there: every request to an ISR route then invokes the edge function, including cache
hits. That is inherent to asking for edge middleware, applies only when
`middlewareMode: 'edge'` is set, and the alternative today is middleware that silently does
not run.

Vercel's native `x-middleware-next` protocol is not a usable alternative here: Astro's `next()`
must return a `Response` so middleware can post-process it, and `x-middleware-next` only hands
off. That is why the adapter generates a full handler that `fetch`es `/_render`.

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://github.com/asmyshlyaev177/astro-isr-middleware-repro

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.

items.title: @astrojs/vercel serverless entrypoint should set duplex when forwarding request bodies

labels.name: - P4: important
labels.description: Violate documented behavior or significantly impacts performance (priority)

items.body:
### Astro Info

```block
Astro: 6.1.8
@astrojs/vercel: 10.0.4
Runtime: Vercel Serverless Functions on Node.js 22
```

I also checked the `@astrojs/vercel@10.0.5` tarball and the generated serverless entrypoint still appears to have the same behavior.

### Describe the Bug

When the Vercel serverless adapter receives a request with a body through the ISR/middleware `realPath` branch, the generated `dist/serverless/entrypoint.js` rebuilds the request with `body: request.body` but without `duplex: "half"`.

On Node 22/Undici this fails at runtime:

```text
TypeError: RequestInit: duplex option is required when sending a body.
    at node:internal/deps/undici/undici:14976:13
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:103:5)
```

The relevant generated code path is:

```js
if (realPath) {
  const url = new URL(request.url);
  url.pathname = realPath;
  request = new Request(url.toString(), {
    method,
    headers,
    body: request.body
  });
}
```

This showed up as repeated production 500s for POST requests routed through the Astro/Vercel serverless function.

The middleware output already handles this correctly in `dist/serverless/middleware.js`:

```js
request = new Request(newRequestUrl, {
  ...request,
  body: request.body,
  duplex: "half"
});
```

### What's the expected result?

The serverless entrypoint should include `duplex: "half"` when forwarding an existing request body, matching the middleware implementation. For example:

```js
request = new Request(url.toString(), {
  method,
  headers,
  body: request.body,
  ...(request.body ? { duplex: "half" } : {})
});
```

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

I do not have a minimal public repo handy, but the failure is visible in the published adapter output for `@astrojs/vercel@10.0.4` and `10.0.5`: any POST request that reaches the `realPath` rewrite branch under Node 22 should reproduce it.

### Participation

- [ ] I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.
